test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Where was Gandhi's method of Satyagraha first evolved and later fully developed as a freedom struggle tool in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**South Africa**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Satyagraha** is a non-violent method of resistance or civil disobedience introduced by **Mahatma Gandhi**.
 
• The method was first conceptualized and practiced in **South Africa** during Gandhi's struggle against racial discrimination. *Hence, this part of the question is correct.*
 
• However, in India, the first significant application of Satyagraha as a tool of freedom struggle took place in **1917** at **Champaran** (currently in Bihar), where Gandhi fought for the rights of indigo farmers being exploited by British planters. 
 
• The success of the **Champaran Satyagraha** made it a model for subsequent movements in **Kheda** (1918), **Ahmedabad Mill Strike** (1918), and other parts of India. *This makes the Champaran movement highly significant in India's freedom struggle.*
 
• While the method was further refined and implemented in various other regions, including **Kheda** and **Bombay**, the foundational development and success of Satyagraha in India are attributed to **Champaran.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Champaran Satyagraha:**

 
 
• The **Champaran Satyagraha** (1917) was initiated to address the grievances of indigo cultivators forced to grow indigo under the **tinkathia system**, wherein farmers were compelled to cultivate indigo on a portion of their land and sell it at prices fixed by the British planters.
 
• Gandhi's leadership and non-violent resistance led to the abolition of the oppressive system, marking a **turning point** in India's freedom struggle.
 
 
 
• **Satyagraha in South Africa:**
 
 
• **Gandhi** first developed the philosophy of Satyagraha during his struggle against racial discrimination in **South Africa** (1893-1914).
 
• His campaigns included resistance to unjust laws like the **Asiatic Registration Act** and the denial of civil rights to Indians in South Africa.
 
 
 
• **Other Movements in India:**
 
 
• **Kheda Satyagraha (1918):** Gandhi supported farmers in Gujarat who were unable to pay taxes due to a famine. The success of this movement further strengthened the idea of non-violent resistance.
 
• **Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918):** Gandhi mediated between workers and mill owners, advocating for wage increases and workers' rights.
 
• **Dandi March (1930):** Another notable application of Satyagraha where Gandhi protested the British salt monopoly through the **Salt Satyagraha.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics of Satyagraha:**

 
 
• It is based on the principle of **non-violence** (ahimsa) and truth (satya).
 
• It involves **civil disobedience, non-cooperation, and peaceful resistance** to unjust laws.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Champaran Satyagraha:**
 
 
• It marked the beginning of **Gandhi's active involvement** in India's freedom struggle.
 
• It inspired other leaders and movements, setting the stage for the **nationalist movement.**
